title: When LLMs Develop Languages: Symbolic Communication for Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning
claim: Prior reasoning approaches use long text or external executors; ours evolves compact shared symbolic languages and routes among them per query.
layout: 3 panels; (a) left comparison stack of baselines vs ours, (b)/(c) right, left-to-right flows
description: A dense three-part diagram. Panel (a), on the left, is a conceptual comparison. A top box shows Input Query and Communicative Router feeding a dynamic pool of LSFs, with the goal of higher accuracy and fewer tokens. Below it, two graph sketches contrast naive-prompt communication (a tangled web of nodes) with LSF-language communication (organized hub-and-spoke). To the right, four stacked flow diagrams compare Standard CoT, Self-consistency, Program-based PoT/PAL and the highlighted dashed CLSR box, each running from query through modules to an answer. Panel (b), top right, shows an evolution loop where agents A and LLMs update symbols S from t to t+1 using training queries. Panel (c), bottom right, shows the test query going to an LLM-router that picks from the LSF pool in one of three cases: pick the best LSF, pick several, or compose a new one. Colors are pastel blue, red, yellow, green and orange.
caption: Communicative Language Symbolism Routing (CLSR). (a) We let LLMs self-evolve an LLM-oriented compact Language Symbolism Framework (LSF), i.e., an information-dense reasoning "dialect", rather than expanding natural language rationales ( e.g., CoT) or relying on an external executor ( e.g., PoT). An LLM router then selects, ensembles, or composes LSFs, enabling a controllable accuracy--token trade-off. (b) Multiple agents iteratively propose, critique, and mutate candidate LSFs based on high-leverage selection. (c) The saturated LSF pool is then queried at inference time for query-adaptive protocol planning.
abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves large language models (LLMs) on difficult reasoning tasks, but it often incurs long natural-language rationales that are poorly aligned with efficient machine reasoning. We propose Communicative Language Symbolism Routing (CLSR), a test-time framework in which multiple LLM agents autonomously invent, evolve, and share compact Language Symbolism Frameworks (LSFs), while a latent-free router adaptively selects and composes these languages per query to optimize the accuracy-token trade-off. Unlike prompt optimization that refines surface instructions, CLSR treats each LSF as a reusable symbolic protocol with compact symbols, usage rules, and a message-passing contract, and improves it through an evolutionary loop driven by correctness and token cost. At inference time, the router may invoke a single low-cost LSF call, ensemble multiple LSFs, or execute a multi-round LSF composition protocol on harder queries. Across challenging benchmarks, CLSR reduces latency-oriented generated token completion by $3\sim 6\times$ compared to standard CoT while maintaining accuracy. We further derive an information-theoretic lower bound on token cost under arbitrary symbolism and show that, under an interpreter-realizability premise, multi-round LSF protocols conditionally subsume program-execution pipelines. Code is publicly available (https://github.com/pzqpzq/LSF_MDia).
